rows.title: Scope
rows.pointer: MduX contributes to a device's security posture without running the standard's process itself — it is a dependency a manufacturer's secure development life cycle would need to account for, not the life cycle.

rows.title: Relationship to IEC 62304
rows.pointer: Maps each IEC 62304 lifecycle activity to its security counterpart, so a manufacturer using MduX runs one process rather than two.

rows.title: Normative references
rows.pointer: Read alongside docs/iso14971/, which covers the risk-management framework a security risk assessment sits inside.

rows.title: Terms and definitions
rows.pointer: Names the security concepts that recur here and where MduX makes each concrete: trust zones, provenance, defect tracking, and build tamper-evidence.

rows.title: One risk file, not two
rows.pointer: MduX's security records use the ISO 14971 risk-record shape, so a security hazard cannot escape the review every safety hazard gets.

rows.title: What MduX does not do
rows.pointer: MduX performs no device-level security risk assessment, for the same reason it performs no device-level safety risk assessment: it has no device.

rows.title: What MduX does supply
rows.pointer: The governed/adapter/tools trust-zone split constrains a governed target's dependency surface at the architecture level - mechanically enforced by MduXTrustZones.cmake at configure time - rather than relying on a runtime security control layered on afterward.

rows.title: The gap this corpus does not paper over
rows.pointer: None of MduX's three mechanisms was designed against this standard; they are inputs to a manufacturer's assessment, not evidence of a completed one.

rows.title: Secure design
rows.pointer: MduX's trust-zone architecture is the clearest instance of a design-time security property in this repository.

rows.title: Secure implementation
rows.pointer: Where MduX ships a derived artifact rather than only source, the consumer verifies it before use.

rows.title: What no MduX mechanism covers
rows.pointer: MduX runs `clang-tidy` and compiles warnings-as-errors, which is general code hygiene rather than a security programme, and has no secrets to handle.

rows.title: Security verification and validation
rows.pointer: MduX verifies two properties this practice cares about - the trust-zone dependency boundary and cross-toolchain byte identity - and fuzzes none of its parsing surfaces, which is a gap rather than a scope exclusion.

rows.title: Vulnerability and defect management
rows.pointer: MduX tracks defects in GitHub Issues, with the general-purpose-tracking limits already set out in [`../iec62304/07-problem-resolution-process.md`](../iec62304/07-problem-resolution-process.md).

rows.title: Security update management
rows.pointer: MduX has no deployed product, so it has no update mechanism to describe — the same honest gap already recorded for maintenance in [`../iec62304/04-maintenance-process.md`](../iec62304/04-maintenance-process.md).

rows.title: Security documentation and guidance
rows.pointer: The caveat stated throughout this directory applies with full force here: none of them was written against IEC 81001-5-1's documentation requirements, so they should be read as material a manufacturer can use, not as a deliverable this standard asks for and MduX has produced.
